documents.unit: Technology Services (ChatGPT Edu for Fresno State)
documents.title: AI Guidelines - ChatGPT Edu for Fresno State
documents.stance_why: The page sets shared principles but says "Each course may have its own rules and expectations regarding AI usage, set by the instructor" and "When permitted by your instructor", so the stance toward AI use is handed to instructors: delegates.
documents.summary: Technology Services guidance for ChatGPT Edu that sets principles (disclosure, accountability, privacy) and tells students that each course's rules are set by the instructor and that AI is used only when permitted. It also gives separate do/do-not lists for faculty on data privacy and grading.

units.why: Principle sentence: AI as "a support rather than a substitute for personal effort"; it tells students how AI may sit alongside their own work, so P32 (student stays primary thinker) fits better than P41, since no skill-building mechanism is explained.
units.anchor: serving as a support rather than a substitute for personal effort, critical thinking

units.why: Tells students to "consult your instructor" to confirm AI "is permitted in the course"; a when-unsure-ask rule (P10), not a syllabus mandate on instructors.
units.anchor: consult your instructor to ensure you are using AI appropriately
units.policy: Students review course guidelines and consult their instructor to make sure AI use is permitted in the course

units.why: Integrity principle: AI must "support independent learning" and not "circumvent academic responsibilities". It is an institution-level principle (P56) rather than a specific prohibition.
units.anchor: AI tools be used in ways that support independent learning

units.why: "must be properly cited, clearly disclosed" is a mandatory disclosure/citation rule for AI-generated content, so P24 (disclose with each submission); no tool/prompt detail is demanded, so not P25.
units.anchor: AI generated content must be properly cited, clearly disclosed

units.why: "Always disclose how AI was used" is an explicit transparency requirement for academic work: P24.
units.anchor: Always disclose how AI was used

units.why: Transparent use "includes recognizing AI's potential limitations or biases and communicating them"; it asks students to name bias, so P53 rather than P31 (which is about verifying output).
units.anchor: recognizing AI’s potential limitations or biases and communicating them
units.policy: Transparent use includes recognizing AI's potential limitations or biases and communicating them

units.why: "You are ultimately responsible for the quality, originality, and integrity of your work, regardless of AI assistance" is the ownership rule: P29.
units.anchor: ultimately responsible for the quality, originality, and integrity of your work

units.why: Students must "critically evaluate, verify, and refine any AI assisted output": verification duty, P31.
units.anchor: critically evaluate, verify, and refine any AI assisted output

units.why: AI "not to gain an unfair advantage or replace collaboration" is a fairness principle without a concrete rule, so P56 (framework principle) rather than P19.
units.anchor: not to gain an unfair advantage or replace collaboration

units.why: "You must not use AI to deceive, fabricate data, or manipulate information" bans deceptive uses; no closed type covers deception or fabrication (P19 is about producing submitted work), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: You must not use AI to deceive, fabricate data, or manipulate information
units.uncovered_note: Prohibition on using AI to deceive, fabricate data or manipulate information.

units.why: "You should not input or share personal, confidential, sensitive data, or intellectual property" is a data-protection rule: P50.
units.anchor: You should not input or share personal, confidential, sensitive data, or intellectual property

units.why: "must align with institutional policies on information security, privacy, and academic integrity" ties AI use to existing policies, a framework statement (P56).
units.anchor: must align with institutional policies on information security, privacy, and academic integrity

units.why: "Do not upload or share personally identifiable information (PII)" is a direct data-protection prohibition for users of ChatGPT Edu: P50.
units.anchor: Do not upload or share personally identifiable information (PII)

units.why: "Do not enter student grades, disciplinary records, or academic performance data into ChatGPT" protects student records; it is a privacy rule for staff, P50.
units.anchor: Do not enter student grades, disciplinary records, or academic performance data into ChatGPT

units.why: "Avoid discussing or inputting any confidential university data, research data, or unpublished findings" is a confidentiality rule: P50.
units.anchor: Avoid discussing or inputting any confidential university data, research data, or unpublished findings

units.why: "Faculty should not use ChatGPT to evaluate student work or generate student grades" keeps grading with humans: P46.
units.anchor: Faculty should not use ChatGPT to evaluate student work or generate student grades

units.why: "Do not distribute ChatGPT-generated content without proper attribution or critical review" requires attribution when sharing output. I chose P24 (attribution) over P31 because the attribution requirement is the stated rule; review is covered in the next unit.
units.anchor: Do not distribute ChatGPT-generated content without proper attribution or critical review

units.why: "may contain inaccuracies or biases. Always verify information before sharing" is a verify-output rule: P31.
units.anchor: Always verify information before sharing

units.why: Instructors are told to "provide guidelines on appropriate vs. inappropriate use" if students may use AI, i.e. state expectations in assignments: P09.
units.anchor: provide guidelines on appropriate vs. inappropriate use

units.why: "Consider requiring students to disclose AI-assisted work and reflect on how they used it" recommends disclosure plus reflection; P26 (reflections) fits better than P24 because reflection is named.
units.anchor: Consider requiring students to disclose AI-assisted work and reflect on how they used it

units.why: "Teach students to evaluate AI-generated content critically, ensuring accuracy, bias detection, and proper citation" asks faculty to build verification skills: P31.
units.anchor: Teach students to evaluate AI-generated content critically

units.why: "Remind students that AI-generated sources may not be reliable and should be fact-checked" is an instructor reminder about verification: P31.
units.anchor: Remind students that AI-generated sources may not be reliable and should be fact-checked

units.why: "Faculty should not input unpublished research, grant proposals, or confidential institutional data into ChatGPT" restricts faculty data sharing: P50.
units.anchor: Faculty should not input unpublished research, grant proposals, or confidential institutional data

units.why: "AI should not be used for automated grading or providing feedback on sensitive academic work" bars automated grading; grading is the headline so P46 (feedback is secondary).
units.anchor: AI should not be used for automated grading or providing feedback on sensitive academic work

units.why: "Use AI as an augmentation to teaching, Not a replacement" says what instructors should use AI for in teaching: P59.
units.anchor: Use AI as an augmentation to teaching, Not a replacement

units.why: Preamble stating the guidelines "reflect shared learning community values to guide ethical AI practices" after naming "over-reliance on AI, reduced critical thinking"; a purpose and principles statement, P56.
units.anchor: These guidelines reflect shared learning community values to guide ethical AI practices in classrooms

units.why: "may result in academic misconduct penalties" classes AI misuse that violates integrity policy as academic misconduct: P36 (no specific penalty named, so not P37).
units.anchor: may result in academic misconduct penalties

units.why: "All use of AI tools must comply with existing university standards, policies, and guidelines" sets compliance with the institution-wide framework: P56.
units.anchor: All use of AI tools must comply with existing university standards, policies, and guidelines

units.why: "Each course may have its own rules and expectations regarding AI usage, set by the instructor" delegates the rule to instructors: P04.
units.anchor: may have its own rules and expectations regarding AI usage, set by the instructor

units.why: "Students should carefully read the syllabus and course materials" points students to the instructor-set rule; I coded it P04 since it is the student side of instructor-set rules and no type covers reading the syllabus.
units.anchor: Students should carefully read the syllabus and course materials

units.why: "students are expected to consult their instructor" when a question arises about appropriate AI use in a course: P10.
units.anchor: students are expected to consult their instructor

units.why: "Course-specific norms are shaped by the unique learning goals and ethical standards of each classroom" says norms are course-specific: P11.
units.anchor: Course-specific norms are shaped by the unique learning goals and ethical standards of each classroom

units.why: "When permitted by your instructor, AI tools can be used like a tutor" with brainstorming, clarifying concepts, summarizing: P12 (tutor), chosen over P15 and P14 because the tutor framing is the main frame.
units.anchor: When permitted by your instructor, AI tools can be used like a tutor

units.why: AI "should not replace active engagement with course material or be used to complete assignments without demonstrating independent learning": keeps student as primary problem-solver, P32.
units.anchor: should not replace active engagement with course material

units.why: "must be clearly acknowledged and not submitted as your original work without proper citation" is a disclosure requirement: P24.
units.anchor: must be clearly acknowledged and not submitted as your original work without proper citation

units.why: "Always apply critical thinking and independent judgment when interpreting AI outputs, and cross-check information" is a verify-output rule: P31.
units.anchor: Always apply critical thinking and independent judgment when interpreting AI outputs

units.why: "AI biases can come from different sources, including" training data, processing methods and user input; names bias concerns: P53.
units.anchor: AI biases can come from different sources

units.why: "Individual user interactions and conversations with ChatGPT are not monitored" describes how the sanctioned tool handles user data: P50 (privacy, vetted tool), informs.
units.anchor: Individual user interactions and conversations with ChatGPT are not monitored

units.why: "OpenAI does not use CSU workspace data to train its large language models" describes the vendor agreement and data limits: P65.
units.anchor: OpenAI does not use CSU workspace data to train its large language models

units.why: "provide advanced AI capabilities for all employees and students" states that the university supplies ChatGPT Edu to everyone: P17.
units.anchor: provide advanced AI capabilities for all employees and students

units.why: "The CSU will continue to update policies, procedures and guidelines as necessary" says policy will change: P54.
units.anchor: The CSU will continue to update policies, procedures and guidelines as necessary

units.why: Violations are handled by "existing standards on student conduct and defined student conduct process": classes misuse as a conduct matter, P36.
units.anchor: existing standards on student conduct and defined student conduct process

units.why: The GenAI Committee "will develop and provide the ongoing guidance for AI in the CSU" names who maintains guidance: P56 (institution-level framework), though it also bears on governance over time.
units.anchor: will develop and provide the ongoing guidance for AI in the CSU

documents.title: Student Terms and Conditions for Use of Generative AI Tools & Solutions
documents.stance_why: "Submission of fully AI-generated content is prohibited unless explicitly allowed by the faculty member" makes banned-unless-permitted the operative rule for submissions, and acceptable uses are limited to "brainstorming, summarizing, or seeking explanations", so restrict; the document does not itself offer tiers.
documents.summary: Click-through terms for students using GenAI for academic work: follow course rules, cite and verify AI output, protect data, and expect conduct-process action for misuse. Fully AI-generated submissions are banned unless the faculty member allows them.

units.why: "students are required to comply with the Policy and Procedures on Cheating and Plagiarism" binds AI use to the cheating policy: P36.
units.anchor: required to comply with the Policy and Procedures on Cheating and Plagiarism

units.why: "Violations will be addressed through the established Student Conduct Process and APM 235" names the enforcement route: P36.
units.anchor: Violations will be addressed through the established Student Conduct Process and APM 235

units.why: By using GenAI students "agree to follow the guidelines outlined in this agreement" and the terms are accepted with a checkbox; no closed type covers a click-through acceptance, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: students agree to follow the guidelines outlined in this agreement
units.uncovered_note: Students must accept a click-through terms agreement before using GenAI tools for academic work.

units.why: "Expectations ... may differ between courses and instructors" delegates rules to courses and instructors: P04.
units.anchor: Expectations for the use of Generative AI may differ between courses and instructors

units.why: "Students are responsible for understanding and following the guidelines provided in each course syllabus, assignment description, or related communication" puts the burden on students to follow instructor-set rules: P04 (no closer type).
units.anchor: Students are responsible for understanding and following the guidelines provided in each course

units.why: "When in doubt, students should consult their instructors directly": ask-first rule, P10.
units.anchor: When in doubt, students should consult their instructors directly

units.why: "GenAI use must not conflict with any existing institutional standards, academic policies, or conduct guidelines" links AI use to existing rules: P56.
units.anchor: GenAI use must not conflict with any existing institutional standards, academic policies, or conduct guidelines

units.why: "When in doubt, ask your professor before using any GenAI tools, even if those tools are available through Fresno State": ask-before-using rule, P10.
units.anchor: When in doubt, ask your professor before using any GenAI tools

units.why: "these guidelines are subject to change" says the policy will be revised: P54.
units.anchor: these guidelines are subject to change

units.why: "Students are responsible for staying informed and adapting to updates" is the student duty tied to policy change; P54 covers change, but the duty is placed on students.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for staying informed and adapting to updates

units.why: "must not be used in any way that violates the university's academic integrity or plagiarism policies" ties AI use to integrity policy: P36.
units.anchor: not be used in any way that violates the university’s academic integrity or plagiarism policies

units.why: "Submission of fully AI-generated content is prohibited unless explicitly allowed by the faculty member": default ban on submitting AI output as own work, P19 (the exception is instructor permission).
units.anchor: Submission of fully AI-generated content is prohibited unless explicitly allowed by the faculty member

units.why: "should never be submitted as original student work without appropriate citation or acknowledgment, where allowed" is a citation requirement: P24.
units.anchor: should never be submitted as original student work without appropriate citation or acknowledgment

units.why: "failure to cite or disclose its use, may constitute plagiarism" makes nondisclosure the violation: P28.
units.anchor: failure to cite or disclose its use, may constitute plagiarism

units.why: "Students must verify the accuracy of all AI-generated content before using or citing it": P31.
units.anchor: Students must verify the accuracy of all AI-generated content before using or citing it

units.why: "to fabricate data, mislead instructors, or cheat in academic assessments is strictly prohibited" bans deceptive uses; cheating in assessments is broader than P22 exam bans and fabrication has no type, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: to fabricate data, mislead instructors, or cheat in academic assessments is strictly prohibited
units.uncovered_note: Prohibition on using AI to fabricate data, mislead instructors or cheat in assessments.

units.why: "AI-generated content can be inaccurate or misleading (often described as hallucinations)" warns about wrong output: P31.
units.anchor: AI-generated content can be inaccurate or misleading

units.why: "must be cross-checked with reliable academic or professional sources before use" is a verify duty: P31.
units.anchor: must be cross-checked with reliable academic or professional sources before use

units.why: "GenAI systems will reflect the bias present in their training data" names bias: P53.
units.anchor: GenAI systems will reflect the bias present in their training data

units.why: AI "should be used as a learning aid" and not a replacement for "student engagement, independent thinking" keeps the student as thinker: P32.
units.anchor: AI tools should be used as a learning aid

units.why: "Acceptable uses include brainstorming, summarizing, or seeking explanations" lists permitted uses; P12 (explanation/tutor) is the lead item, chosen over P15 and P14.
units.anchor: Acceptable uses include brainstorming, summarizing, or seeking explanations

units.why: "not completing assignments or bypassing learning outcomes" rules out having AI complete assignments: P19.
units.anchor: not completing assignments or bypassing learning outcomes

units.why: "may result in disciplinary action for academic misconduct as determined by the course instructor" classes misuse as misconduct and gives the instructor the call: P36.
units.anchor: may result in disciplinary action for academic misconduct

units.why: "Students acknowledge the potential security and privacy risks" states privacy risk: P50.
units.anchor: Students acknowledge the potential security and privacy risks

units.why: "should not input personal, confidential, or sensitive university-related information" is a data-protection rule: P50.
units.anchor: should not input personal, confidential, or sensitive university-related information

units.why: "Use AI tools with caution and in accordance with university data protection standards": P50.
units.anchor: in accordance with university data protection standards

No school, computing or course documents were collected. The student-guidelines text is extracted one word per line; anchors were matched across line breaks.
